newsitem.title: USA: Assessments up in Boston's affluent neighborhoods.
newsitem.headline: Assessments up in Boston's affluent neighborhoods.

text.p: After nearly a decade of flat or decreasing property values, homeowners in Boston's affluent communites are finding their property values - and tax assessments - are up sharply, according to a report in the Boston Globe Monday.

Case Shiller Weiss, Inc of Cambridge, Mass., whose index tracks and analyzes repeat home sales, finds that in some of the affluent suburbs of Boston, Wellesley, Brookline and Newton, values of homes are up 31 percent from the bottom of the market several years ago and prices have increased 20 percent from their 1988 prices, the newspaper reported.

Proposition 2, a 15-year-old cap on local property taxes, means communities are restricted from increasing their total intake, known as a tax levy, by more than two percent annually. So if assessments go up significantly, cities and towns must lower their tax rates to stay under that cap.

There are two alternatives. A community can vote for an override to increase the levy or the local government can shfit the tax burden - businesses pay lower rate, while homeowners pay a higher rate, the Globe said.
